purpose: Canonical seed layer for central banks, currencies, sovereign and supranational debt, reserve assets, settlement systems, creditor classes, cross-border claims and financial obligations. It is designed to answer who issues, who owes, who holds, in what currency, through which institution, at what date, and with what evidence.
boundary: This file is an empirical finance layer. Tim/Potatoverse Axis geography remains a separate project-interpretive overlay. A country appearing in a North aggregation does not imply sovereignty, legal authority, consent, ownership or political control. Monetary membership, debt holdings, custody, settlement links and lending relationships must never be silently converted into Axis membership or authority claims.
modeling_principles: Separate monetary authority from fiscal issuer: a central bank can set monetary policy while national treasuries issue sovereign debt.
Separate issuer from holder: the debtor is the issuer; a creditor is a holder or lender only to the extent supported by the instrument or claim data.
Separate custody location from beneficial ownership: TIC and similar custody-based datasets can misidentify the ultimate beneficial owner.
Separate central-government debt, general-government debt, debt held by the public, gross debt, net debt and external debt.
Separate a security funding leg from a downstream loan leg: an investor buying an ESM or EU bond is not automatically a direct creditor of the final programme beneficiary.
Keep currency denomination distinct from economic exposure and from the nationality of creditor or debtor.
Every numeric observation retains concept, unit, reference period, source and evidence status.
Missing counterparty detail is represented as unknown or an aggregate creditor class rather than guessed.

debt_concepts.label: General government gross debt
debt_concepts.scope: Consolidated gross debt of general government under the applicable statistical framework.

debt_concepts.label: Central government debt
debt_concepts.scope: Debt of central government; excludes other general-government subsectors unless the source explicitly consolidates them.

debt_concepts.label: U.S. federal debt held by the public
debt_concepts.scope: Treasury definition: federal debt held outside federal government accounts, including domestic and foreign holders and Federal Reserve Banks.

debt_concepts.label: U.S. total public debt outstanding
debt_concepts.scope: Debt held by the public plus intragovernmental holdings under U.S. Treasury reporting.

debt_concepts.label: Debt securities outstanding
debt_concepts.scope: Tradable debt instruments such as bills, commercial paper, negotiable certificates of deposit, bonds and debentures; BIS datasets distinguish domestic and international markets.

debt_concepts.label: Cross-border bank claim
debt_concepts.scope: Banking-system claim reported under BIS international banking statistics; not the same thing as sovereign debt.

debt_concepts.label: Official reserve assets
debt_concepts.scope: Reserve assets held by monetary authorities. IMF COFER publishes allocated reserve currency composition in aggregate and keeps individual economy submissions confidential.

debt_concepts.label: Custody-reported foreign holdings of U.S. Treasury securities
debt_concepts.scope: TIC country attribution based primarily on custodial location; it is not guaranteed to identify the ultimate beneficial owner.

central_banks.name: Federal Reserve System
central_banks.structure: Board of Governors plus 12 Federal Reserve Banks; monetary-policy decisions are made through the Federal Open Market Committee.

central_banks.name: European Central Bank / Eurosystem
central_banks.structure: The Eurosystem is the ECB plus the national central banks of euro-area countries; the wider ESCB also includes EU national central banks outside the euro area.

central_banks.name: Danmarks Nationalbank
central_banks.structure: Denmark retains the krone and operates a fixed-exchange-rate policy against the euro. Danmarks Nationalbank manages central-government borrowing and debt on behalf of the Minister of Finance.

currency_systems.name: United States dollar
currency_systems.regime_note: National currency of the United States; also widely used internationally as a reserve, invoicing and funding currency.

currency_systems.name: Euro
currency_systems.regime_note: Single currency of 21 EU member states as of 1 January 2026; national fiscal issuers remain distinct.

sovereign_and_supranational_issuers.name: United States Department of the Treasury
Euro-area national fiscal issuers
sovereign_and_supranational_issuers.modeling_note: The ECB is the monetary authority for EUR, but sovereign bonds remain liabilities of their respective national issuers unless an instrument is explicitly supranational.

sovereign_and_supranational_issuers.name: European Commission EU-Bonds
sovereign_and_supranational_issuers.modeling_note: EU-Bonds fund EU programmes under the Commission's unified funding approach. They are not interchangeable with a member state's national sovereign bonds.

sovereign_and_supranational_issuers.name: European Stability Mechanism
sovereign_and_supranational_issuers.modeling_note: The ESM raises funds from markets and can lend to ESM members. Model the ESM security and the downstream ESM loan as separate obligations.

settlement_and_infrastructure.name: Norway / Eurosystem settlement integration track
settlement_and_infrastructure.note: Norges Bank has formal work with the ECB around Eurosystem settlement infrastructure, including an agreement to use the Eurosystem platform for instant payments. This is a financial-infrastructure relationship, not euro-area membership.

north_axis_bridge.boundary: North is a project-defined analytical lens only. Finance records remain unchanged and independently sourced when viewed through it.
planned_queries: Which project-North jurisdictions share the euro and which retain national currencies?
Which project-North central banks participate directly in Eurosystem infrastructure and which connect from outside it?
Which project-North fiscal issuers issue in their own monetary currency and which borrow in foreign currencies?
Which creditor sectors and countries hold each sovereign or supranational security when the evidence can resolve them?
What cross-border bank claims run between project-North jurisdictions and the rest of the world?
What reserve-currency exposures and settlement dependencies are visible without inferring confidential country portfolios?
How much debt is central-government, general-government, supranational, bank, household or corporate rather than collapsing all obligations into one total?
Which obligations mature when, in which currency, and through which clearing or settlement infrastructure?
